transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

They... my lieutenant sent me here. I was at the station. Just moving the airway bags around. I had to put them in a pattern I knew was right. And... I was repeating the dispatch numbers out loud. 

He told me to stop and step away, but I wouldn't. I couldn't. If I broke the sequence... the whole bay would go bad. So they made me come here.
When you say the whole bay would go bad, did you know that might just be your mind telling you that, or were you certain it would really happen?

It wasn't my mind. I was certain. 

Because I... I already know what they're doing to me. The injury review people. Some of the supervisors, too. They've been watching me through the station cameras. And they... they go in and change my triage notes. Just to make me look unsafe. They keep telling me it's just routine paperwork, but... I know. I know they're doing it. So, yeah. I was certain.
Have you been hearing voices when no one is there?
No. I don't... no. I haven't heard anything like that. Just the people who are actually there.
Before this started, did the urge to arrange the bags and repeat the numbers feel intrusive and unwanted to you?
No. I don't... I don't really know what you mean by intrusive. It wasn't unwanted. I just... I had to do it. That's all.
Do you feel that anyone can put thoughts into your mind or take thoughts out of it?
No. I don't... no. Nobody's putting things in my head. They're just watching me. That's all.
Do you believe the cameras are being used to do something impossible, like transmit messages or signals directly into you?
No. I don't... they aren't sending signals or anything like that. They just... they just record what I'm doing. That's it.
Do you believe arranging the bags and repeating the numbers makes sense, or does any part of you think it might not?
It makes sense to me. I don't... I don't think it's wrong or anything. It's just what I have to do.
How long have you been sure that the injury review people and supervisors are watching you and changing your triage notes?
About two months. That's... that's when the camera and the paperwork stuff started. And the things at the station that got everyone all alarmed. Just the last two months or so.
Did this all come on suddenly, over a few days?
I'm not... I don't really know. It just sort of... happened. I wasn't keeping track of the days or anything.
For more than one month now, have you been continuously sure that the supervisors and injury review people are watching you and changing your notes?

Yeah. Like I said... it's been about two months. That's how long the camera and the paperwork stuff has been happening... and the things at the station that got everyone so alarmed. So, yeah, more than a month.
Since this started, have you been able to do your job as usual?

No. I... I can't work the ambulance anymore. They put me on desk duty for a bit, just doing notes and equipment checks, but... they said I was unreliable. So they took me off the schedule. I don't really go in now. I've mostly just... stopped seeing friends, too. Haven't been keeping up with things around the house much either. Just... keeping to myself.
From when these problems first began up to today, has it been less than three months?
No... it's been longer. It all started... well, I hurt my shoulder and my ribs. It was during an ambulance transfer. That was... about eight months ago. So, no, it's been longer than three.
For the past three months, have you been continuously sure that the supervisors and injury review people are watching you and changing your notes?
No... I told you. The camera stuff... it's only been about two months. Not three.
When you talk, do people tell you that your thoughts jump around or that what you say is hard to follow?
No. I... I don't think so. Like I said, I don't really talk to people much right now anyway. But... no, no one's told me that.
Since these beliefs started, have there been any days when you no longer believed the supervisors were watching you and changing your notes?
No. They're always doing it. I haven't had a day where they weren't.
Since this started, have you had a period of feeling unusually high, energized, or euphoric?
No. I haven't... I don't feel like that.

patient.answer:

Also included autism spectrum and anankastic personality traits as possible contributors to rigid patterns/rituals, though current data are insufficient.

patient.answer: No. I don't... they aren't sending signals or anything like that. They just... they just record what I'm doing. That's it.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a fixed, non-bizarre persecutory delusion that supervisors and injury review staff are watching him through cameras and altering his triage notes, held with full conviction for about two months without remission. There are no hallucinations, thought insertion/withdrawal, disorganization, or manic symptoms. OCD is less likely because the repetitive behaviors were not experienced as intrusive or unwanted and were considered fully sensible. Acute psychotic disorder was considered but the delusional belief has persisted beyond 1 month and the presentation is most consistent with a persistent delusional disorder, persecutory type.
